chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) passed by a man who had a garment with him that he was selling. The man was tall and the garment was short, so he (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'Sit down, for it is more beneficial for your commodity.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ethical ruling on displaying goods for sale in Islam?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi illustrates the Prophetic practice of *tadlis* (strategic presentation) in commerce, where physical positioning is used to enhance the perceived value of goods without deception. It underscores the Shia emphasis on ethical trade practices, balancing commercial advantage with transparency, a principle further elaborated by scholars like Al-Shaykh al-Mufid in discussions on market ethics.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> passed by a man and with him were clothes he was selling, and the man was tall and the cloth was short, so he<sup>saww</sup> said to him: ‘Be seated, for it is more beneficial for your commodity’.
en.sarwar: 35. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, once passed by a man who sold clothes. The man was tall and the cloth was short. He (the Messenger of Allah) said, ‘Sit down; it is more useful for your commodity.”’
